f1.quote: The alloy was heated in situ from room temperature to 1100 °C under either low-oxygen/vacuum or atmospheric-air conditions while HTXRD tracked phase and oxide evolution

f2.quote: under either low-oxygen/vacuum or atmospheric-air conditions

f3.quote: Heating proceeded at 10 °C/min in 50 °C increments, with a 5 min hold at each setpoint

f4.quote: The vacuum was reported as approximately 4.2×10^-6 atm overall pressure, with another section estimating p(O2)=8.82×10^-7 atm; oxygen partial pressure was not measured directly.

f5.quote: FCC appeared around 550–600 °C, sigma around 600–650 °C, and sigma diminished/disappeared around 950–1050 °C.

f6.quote: Selective oxidation occurred primarily by outward diffusion of Al, and secondarily Cr, to react with oxygen.

f7.quote: Oxidation generated an Al-rich external Al2O3 scale with a Cr-rich/Cr2O3 inner region; air produced a thick duplex scale

f8.quote: air produced a thick duplex scale and a pronounced Al-depleted, FCC/B2-denuded subsurface zone, whereas vacuum produced a much thinner scale and thin transformed subsurface layer.

f9.quote: air was expected to produce earlier/more extensive oxidation, a thicker Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale, and stronger Al-depletion-induced subsurface transformation

f12.quote: vacuum exposure was expected to retain only a thin, predominantly alumina protective film.
